predecessors.note: Arghun infobox: 'Preceded by Samma dynasty; Langah Sultanate'.

land.text: Multan, which 'fell in 1528 after an extended siege'

predecessors.note: Taken eight years after the dynasty's start, so it is a gain in the ledger (1528), not part of the birth land.

land.text: Sindh, which the Tarkhan dynasty 'ruled from 1554'; 'Muhammad 'Isa Tarkhan would keep lower Sindh, with his capital at Thatta' while Sultan Mahmud ruled upper Sindh from Bakhar

successors.note: No dossier for the Tarkhans exists yet (counterparts_needing_dossiers in the g-sa-b report). The Arghun page gives no year for the split of Sindh between 'Isa Tarkhan and Sultan Mahmud, only that peace followed 1555 and preceded 'Isa's death in 1567.

capitals.name: Bukkur (Bhakkar, at Sukkur)
capitals.note: Infobox capital 'Bukkur'; text: 'Shah Beg Arghun made Bukkur (Lower Sindh) his official capital.' The page gives no years, so the dynasty's span is used, and it calls Bukkur 'Lower Sindh' although it stands in upper Sindh. Coordinates are the gazetteer's Sukkur (no Bukkur entry).

rulers.name: Shah Beg Arghun
rulers.note: Shah Beg Arghun page infobox: 'Reign: 21 December 1520 - 26 June 1524'; the Arghun page: 'He died in 1524'.

rulers.name: Shah Husayn Arghun
rulers.note: 'He died in 1524 and his son Shah Husayn succeeded him'; Muhammad 'Isa Tarkhan was installed 'as their ruler in 1554' and Shah Husayn 'was set aside and died childless in 1556'. The Arghun page's lower infobox says 'Monarchy 1524-1555'.

correction.text: Sindh as Cliopatria drew it for the Sammas (123,201 km2), the whole of the land Shah Beg took in 1520

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria has no Arghun row and keeps the Samma outline to 1525. The page: 'In 1520 ... he invaded Sindh' and 'Shah Beg gained control of the whole region'. The page gives no area (the infobox has none; the text only says the dynasty 'ruled over the area adjoining Southern Afghanistan and then Sindh'), so there is no infobox figure to compare with the Samma shape's 123,201 km2. The page's own account is muddled: it has Shah Beg gain 'the upper half of Sindh (Thatta)' while the Sammas kept 'the lower half (Bukkur)', then says he took the whole region; the whole of Sindh is drawn.

correction.text: Sindh plus Multan: 'Multan fell in 1528 after an extended siege and Shah Husayn appointed a governor of the city'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Sindh with the Multan radius (170 km, the same disc the Langah dossier uses) added for the two years the Arghuns held the city. The page gives no extent for the Multan country.

correction.text: Sindh again, after the governor of Multan was 'thrown out of the city' and the city went to rebels (Langah page)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Multan leaves the Arghuns by 1530 (bridging year; neither page dates the expulsion). From then to 1554 the Arghun domain is Sindh alone. The Arghun page ends the dynasty at 1554 with Muhammad 'Isa Tarkhan installed 'as their ruler in 1554'.

region.text: Sindh, from Thatta to the north

ledger.note: 1520: Shah Beg Arghun invades Sindh. 'In 1520, in the hopes of establishing a new power base, he invaded Sindh'; the Samma dossier records the same campaign (the Samma page puts it in 926 AH, 1519).

1520: Jam Feroz is beaten and Thatta sacked. 'Shah Beg defeated Jam Feroz's army and proceeded to sack Thatta.' The Shah Beg Arghun page: 'overcame and defeated Jam Feroz, the last ruler of the Samma dynasty, in 1520'.

region.text: Sindh, the realm of the Sammas, now under Shah Beg

ledger.note: 1520: Shah Beg Arghun founds the Arghun dynasty in Sindh. Infobox 'Arghun dynasty begins: 1520'; 'This marked the end of Samma rule in Sindh, as Shah Beg gained control of the whole region.' The month is the start of his reign on the Shah Beg Arghun page ('21 December 1520'), the Arghun page gives only the year.

1525: the Arghuns move on Multan (bridging year). The page says Shah Husayn (succeeded 1524) 'attacked Multan, capital of the Langah Sultanate, probably at Babur's insistence' and gives no year for the start; the Langah dossier uses 1525 and the Langah page puts Husayn II's reign at 1525-1527.
1528: Multan falls. 'Multan fell in 1528 after an extended siege and Shah Husayn appointed a governor of the city.'

region.text: Multan, capital of the Langah Sultanate

ledger.note: 1528: Shah Husayn Arghun takes Multan. 'Multan fell in 1528 after an extended siege'; the Langah page names the governor, his son Mirza Askari, and dates the annexation 1527 in its lead (1528 in its body).

region.text: Multan, whose governor 'was thrown out of the city'

ledger.counterpart: Langah rebels of Multan (Sultan Mahmud II)
ledger.note: 1530 (bridging year): Multan is lost to rebels. Langah page: 'the governor was thrown out of the city' and 'The rebels under Sultan Mahmud II administered Multan for a time independently', with 'autonomous authority until its merger with the Mughal Empire in 1530'; the Arghun page adds that the rebels 'soon afterward submitted to the Mughal Empire'. Neither page dates the expulsion, so 1530 (the Langah page's end of autonomy, the Multan Subah) is the bridge; Sher Shah took Multan in 1541 per the Langah page.

1554: Arghun rule ends in Sindh. Tarkhan page: 'Tarkhan dynasty begins: 1554', 'General Mirza Isa Beg, a Tarkhan, founded the dynasty after the death of Shah Husayn Arghun', after a civil war between Shah Husayn 'and his nobles under Mirza Muhammad 'Isa Tarkhan'; Arghun infobox 'ends: 1554'. The Tarkhan page's table gives 'Monarchy 1555-1591'; the Arghun page's lower infobox 'Monarchy 1524-1555'.

wars.name: Arghun conquest of Sindh
wars.outcome: Shah Beg Arghun defeats Jam Feroz, sacks Thatta and ends Samma rule in Sindh.
wars.note: No Wikipedia article of its own; the Samma page dates the battle to 926 AH (1519), the Arghun and Shah Beg pages to 1520.

wars.name: Arghun conquest of Multan
wars.outcome: Multan falls in 1528 after an extended siege and an Arghun governor is installed; the city is lost again within about two years.
wars.note: Start year 1525 is a bridge (the page dates only the fall); the Langah page says the sultanate was 'annexed in 1527' in its lead and gives 1528 for the fall in its body.

wars.name: Tarkhan seizure of power in Sindh
wars.outcome: After a civil war between Shah Husayn Arghun and his nobles under Muhammad 'Isa Tarkhan, the Tarkhans rule Sindh from 1554 and Shah Husayn is set aside.
wars.note: The page gives no year for the fighting itself, only the dynasty's start at 1554; no zone is named, so none is contested.

certainty.note: No page opened gives a frontier of the Arghun domain; Sindh is drawn as Cliopatria's Samma outline and Multan as a radius. The Thar desert and Baluch edges are approximate.

notes: No Cliopatria row: the Samma outline runs to 1525 and nothing follows it until Mughal Sindh in 1595 (Mughal dossier note), so the Arghun and Tarkhan years 1525-1591 have no Cliopatria shape. Sindh is drawn as the Samma outline of 1521; Multan as the 170 km disc of the Langah dossier. The Arghun page's upper/lower Sindh wording is self-contradictory (Thatta 'upper', Bukkur 'lower'); the whole of Sindh is drawn. The family held Kandahar and Zamindawar before 1520 (page: 'In 1522 Babur took Kandahar after a drawn-out siege and annexed it'; Dhu'l-Nun Beg 'killed in battle against the Uzbeks' in 1507); that earlier principality is outside this dossier's 1520 start and needs its own dossier or a Cliopatria shape if the map should show Kandahar 1479-1522. After 1554: the Tarkhan dynasty (1554-1591/1593 per the two pages) needs a dossier (the Mughal dossier already cites 'Jani Beg (Sindh)' as the 1591 counterpart); the Arghun page also says upper Sindh was annexed by Akbar in 1573. Multan 1528-1541 is the weakest stretch: Arghun governor, rebels under Mahmud II, 'merger with the Mughal Empire in 1530' (Langah page), then Sher Shah in 1541 (Sur dossier gain, holder unnamed); the Langah dossier ends 1528 while the Langah infobox says 1530.
